claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**First, I need to know about the child(ren) you're claiming for:**

1. **How many children are you enquiring about?**
2. **What is the age (or ages) of the child/children?** 

Child Benefit eligibility depends on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualifying
- **16 to 19**: Depends on education or training status
- **20 or over**: Not eligible

Please tell me about each child so we can work through the eligibility check together!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my daughter Alex - she's 17 and still in sixth form doing her A-levels. Does that help?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. That's very helpful context.

So I'm assessing eligibility for:
- **Alex, age 17, in sixth form studying A-levels**

Since Alex is 16-19 years old, I need to check whether she's in qualifying education or training. The good news is that being in sixth form doing A-levels typically qualifies as full-time education, but let me work through the specific requirements with you.

Let me navigate to the next stage of the assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to confirm: **Is Alex currently in education or training?**

From what you've said, she's in sixth form doing A-levels, so it sounds like she is. Just to be clear:

- **In education or training** = Currently enrolled and attending a qualifying education/training course (like school, college, university, apprenticeship, etc.)
- **Left education recently** = Has left within the last 20 weeks and might qualify under an extension
- **Neither** = Not in education/training and hasn't recently left

Please confirm that Alex is currently in education/training (sixth form A-levels), or let me know if her situation is different.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - she's currently in education. She's at sixth form college doing her A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Thank you for confirming that Alex is currently in education at sixth form college doing A-levels.

Now let me move to the next stage to check the specific education level requirements:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check the education level requirements. Based on the criteria, I can see that:

**A-levels ARE approved (non-advanced) education** ✓

This is good news! However, I need to confirm a few details about Alex's A-level course:

1. **Is Alex studying A-levels on a full-time basis?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)

2. **Is this A-level course employer-funded or part of an agreement with an employer about a future job?** (If it's just regular sixth form A-levels, the answer would be no)

3. **Is Alex married?** (This would affect eligibility for 16-19 year olds unless they're financially dependent on you)

Please confirm these details so we can proceed!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She's studying full-time at sixth form - definitely more than 12 hours a week of classes and supervised study. It's just regular A-levels through the college, nothing to do with an employer. And no, she's not married - she lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for confirming all of that. So Alex meets all the education level requirements:

✓ A-levels (approved non-advanced education)
✓ Full-time study (well over 12 hours per week)
✓ Not employer-funded
✓ Not married

Now let me move to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to ask about Alex's work situation:

**Does Alex work, and if so, how many hours per week?**

The rule is that 16-19 year olds in approved education (like Alex) can still receive Child Benefit as long as they're working **less than 24 hours per week** (or not working at all).

So please let me know:
- Is Alex not working, or
- Is she working part-time with **less than 24 hours per week**, or
- Is she working **24 hours or more per week**?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. She's focused on her studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's great. So Alex:

✓ Is in approved education (A-levels)
✓ Studying full-time with adequate supervised study hours
✓ Not working

Now let me proceed to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to ask:

**Is Alex receiving any of the following benefits in her own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit (as an individual claimant)?

Based on what you've told me (she's a student living at home with you), I would expect the answer is no, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she doesn't receive any benefits in her own name. She's just a student living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's clear. Alex doesn't receive any benefits in her own name.

Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship of any kind?**

Since she's doing A-levels at sixth form college, I would expect the answer is no, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not doing an apprenticeship. She's just doing her A-levels at college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship, she's just doing A-levels.

Now let me move to the next stage, which is checking your (the claimant's) residency and working status:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status, as you're the claimant. There are several paths that can qualify:

**Which of the following best describes your situation:**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (most common)
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:
   - You're working (and earning/expect to earn above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months), OR
   - You're actively seeking work, OR
   - You have sufficient resources and aren't claiming Income Support/JSA/Pension Credit/Universal Credit, OR
   - You're a student with sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA/Swiss national
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

Please let me know which applies to you!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's straightforward. You normally live in the UK, which meets the residency requirement.

Let me proceed to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. Responsibility means:

**Which of these applies to you:**

1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already confirmed - you live in Manchester together), OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc. - at least the amount of Child Benefit), OR
3. **You're paying maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Based on what you've told me - that you live at home together in Manchester - it sounds like you definitely meet this requirement (you live with her). But please confirm that you're responsible for her care and upkeep.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me in Manchester. I'm responsible for her care - I provide everything she needs, her food, clothes, housing, all of that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's very clear. You live with Alex and you're responsible for her care and upkeep - you provide her food, clothes, housing, and everything she needs.

Let me proceed to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to ask:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or might anyone else be claiming or planning to claim for her?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming for her?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent or other family member) claiming for her?
- Are you and someone else in dispute about who should claim?

Please let me know the situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm her parent and she lives with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's clear - you're the only person claiming for Alex.

Let me proceed to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex:**
1. **In hospital** (long-term), OR
2. **In care** (local authority care), OR
3. **Fostered**, OR
4. **Living normally at home with you in Manchester** (which is what you've already told me)

Based on what you've said, I believe she's living normally at home with you. Please confirm!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - she's living normally at home with me in Manchester. She's not in hospital, care, or fostered - just a normal teenager living at home while she does her A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's clear - Alex is living normally at home with you.

Let me proceed to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! We're almost at the end. Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the council paying for her housing, food, or other upkeep? (If yes, you may not be eligible)
- Or are you covering all her costs yourself? (If yes, you are eligible)

Based on what you've told me - that you live together and you provide everything she needs - I expect the answer is that the council is NOT paying. Please confirm!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm covering all her costs myself - her accommodation, food, everything she needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's excellent news. You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex!

Let me now proceed to confirm the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! I'm delighted to confirm that you are **ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**! 

Let me now provide you with the formal outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **✅ RESULT: YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

### Summary for Alex:
You are eligible to receive Child Benefit for your 17-year-old daughter Alex because she meets all the qualifying requirements as a 16-19 year old in approved full-time education (A-levels).

### Key Points:
- ✅ Alex is in approved education (A-levels) - not advanced education
- ✅ Full-time study with adequate supervised hours
- ✅ Not working 24+ hours per week
- ✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You're responsible for her care and maintenance
- ✅ No other claimant for Alex
- ✅ Living at home, not in hospital or care
- ✅ Council not paying for her support

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at [www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim) or **by post using form CH2**

2. **You'll need to provide:**
   - Proof of your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of her date of birth

3. **Important note - High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   If you or your partner earns more than £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge, which means you may need to pay back some or all of the benefit through tax. If you earn over £60,000 but under £80,000, you'll pay back 1% of the benefit for each £100 earned. Above £80,000, you pay back the full amount.

4. **Payment arrangements:**
   Payments are made every 4 weeks, usually by bank transfer.

Congratulations! If you have any other questions about Child Benefit, feel free to ask or visit the official gov.uk website for more information.

arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant is eligible to receive Child Benefit for their 17-year-old daughter Alex. Alex meets all the qualifying criteria as a 16-19 year old in approved full-time education (A-levels). The claimant meets all residency requirements (normally resident in the UK), is responsible for Alex's care and upkeep, and is the sole claimant for the child. There are no disqualifying factors present."
